message:
## Vulnerability Digest

**Scan window:** 2026-11-08 05:10 IST to 2026-11-09 05:10 IST (2026-11-07 23:40 to 2026-11-08 23:40 UTC)  
**Scope:** `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt` only, combined and deduplicated. `DLL_software_component.txt` was not read or combined.

No newly reported vulnerability was confirmed as a direct match to the monitored product names during this window. Four low-severity CVEs affecting Secure Custom Fields, a fork of the monitored Advanced Custom Fields plugin, are plausible environment matches and need an installed-product check.

### Possible matches needing review

**Secure Custom Fields before 6.9.8 — CVE-2026-97192**  
- **Severity:** Low, CVSS 3.1 score 2.7 (CISA ADP secondary assessment)
- **Description:** A contributor-level user can save custom fields that the site intended to restrict to administrators.
- **Why it may be relevant:** The inventory names Advanced Custom Fields. WordPress documents that Secure Custom Fields is an ACF fork and that some WordPress.org-managed ACF installations were automatically switched to SCF. The CVE record names SCF, not ACF, so confirm the installed plugin identity.
- **Source:** [NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-97192)

**Secure Custom Fields before 6.9.8 — CVE-2026-97193**  
- **Severity:** Low, CVSS 3.1 score 2.7 (CISA ADP secondary assessment)
- **Description:** Bidirectional relationship synchronization can let a contributor modify references on posts, users, or terms they cannot otherwise edit.
- **Why it may be relevant:** Same ACF-to-SCF product-family relationship; applicability depends on whether an ACF installation was switched to SCF.
- **Source:** [NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-97193)

**Secure Custom Fields before 6.9.8 — CVE-2026-97194**  
- **Severity:** Low, CVSS 3.1 score 2.7 (CISA ADP secondary assessment)
- **Description:** A contributor can disclose titles and non-public statuses of other users' unpublished posts through relational fields.
- **Why it may be relevant:** Same ACF-to-SCF product-family relationship; applicability depends on the installed plugin.
- **Source:** [NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-97194)

**Secure Custom Fields before 6.9.8 — CVE-2026-97195**  
- **Severity:** Low, CVSS 3.1 score 3.5 (CISA ADP secondary assessment)
- **Description:** Insufficient sanitization of a stored field definition can allow script execution in another user's browser when the affected field is rendered.
- **Why it may be relevant:** Same ACF-to-SCF product-family relationship; applicability depends on the installed plugin.
- **Source:** [NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-97195)

WordPress's [SCF announcement](https://wordpress.org/news/2024/10/secure-custom-fields/) documents the fork and automatic-switch scenario. The [official SCF plugin changelog](https://wordpress.org/plugins/secure-custom-fields/) identifies 6.9.8 as the security release containing the relevant fixes.

### MongoDB ecosystem sweep

The dedicated sweep covered MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, mongod, mongos, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, mongosh, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, official drivers and libraries, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm and App Services, official integrations, MongoDB-owned advisories, NVD/CVE records, GitHub advisories, and CISA sources. No new MongoDB-related advisory or CVE was verified inside the scan window. The entries visible on the [official MongoDB alerts page](https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/alerts) and relevant component changelogs predate this window.

**Closing:** No emergency action is indicated by a confirmed direct match. Promptly verify whether any monitored WordPress installation uses Secure Custom Fields; if it does and is below 6.9.8, the four low-severity findings apply and the official security release should be reviewed.
